A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSR/RSR++ research. All pages, figures, tables, equations, and v3 Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching. v2 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original C++ and NumPy timing, memory-consumption, parameter-sensitivity, and RSR-versus-RSR++ experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original Llama3/Falcon3 inference measurements on CPU and GPU, plus GPU matrix-multiplication results.

M1.justification: The core RSR/RSR++ design remains, but v3 adds a CPU/GPU tensor variant using precomputed N = M × Bin[k], reshaping, and batched multiplication (Appendices C.1 and E). Algorithm 3 also drops v2's x ← v update; the unchanged recursive explanation makes this a pseudocode inconsistency rather than an established intended redesign.

E1.justification: Beyond v2's generated binary/ternary matrix inputs, v3 evaluates actual LLM inference using ShortQuestions, SimpleQuestions, and TREC QA (Section 5.3). This substantially extends coverage from isolated multiplication to model execution on question inputs.

E2.justification: The native Standard and NumPy np.dot comparisons remain. v3 additionally evaluates against unmodified PyTorch 1.58-bit models and standard Torch GPU multiplication (Sections 5.3–5.4 and Appendix F.4), adding practical comparators without a broad new algorithm-baseline suite.

E3.justification: v3 introduces single-token, single-feedforward CPU evaluations of Llama3-8B and Falcon3-3B/10B, plus GPU model timing and GPU multiplication over sizes 2^11–2^14. These are substantial new evaluation protocols; the retained C++ and NumPy protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing k-sensitivity and RSR-versus-RSR++ analyses are retained in Appendices F.1–F.2. v3 adds a limited correctness check of model-response equality and a matching 'Paris' response example (Section 5.3 and Appendix E.1).

E5.justification: v3 Table 1 explicitly reports GPU LLM timing means with standard deviations. The existing averages over 10 C++ runs and four NumPy runs remain unchanged; v3 does not specify the GPU repeat count or establish increased repetition of existing experiments.

E6.justification: The retained C++ and NumPy results keep their values. New Figure 6 reports, for example, Falcon3-3B ShortQuestions timings of 96.9 versus 18.5 seconds (5.24x). Table 1 adds GPU model timings, and Figure 12 reports new GPU multiplication speedups decreasing from 2.87x to 1.53x. These are additional results under new settings.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds explicit parallel-time bounds, including O(n^2/(c log n)) for RSR++ using c cores, and mathematical definitions for the tensor formulation. The original decomposition, correctness proof, and sequential complexity arguments are substantially retained and relocated.

C1.justification: The central algorithmic and compression claims remain. v3's abstract distinguishes the retained 29x multiplication speedup from a newly claimed 5.24x LLM inference speedup, while the introduction removes v2's speculative 13x GPT-3 inference estimate.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies practical applicability: Section 5.3 explicitly states that its PyTorch LLM implementation provides no memory reduction, and Appendix D.2 adds hardware-optimization overhead and small-matrix limitations. The explicit v2 caveats about RSR++ sequentiality and time-intensive preprocessing disappear, although block-parallelization discussion is retained elsewhere.

D1.justification: v3 adds model-weight links, server specifications, PyTorch implementation details, four code listings, and synthetic-question construction information (Section 5.3 and Appendix E). It also replaces the GitHub code link with an anonymous-repository link. This substantially expands documented implementation and access information.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds binary/ternary quantization and fast-multiplication references, plus an explicit comparison with Four Russians' Boolean matrix-matrix multiplication. The existing application-level, hardware-independent positioning remains. These cited methods are not newly reported experimental baselines.

P1.justification: v3 extensively reorganizes the narrative: background, proofs, discussion, and several experiments move into appendices; related-work and implementation sections are introduced; and the abstract, introduction, contribution summary, and solution overview are revised.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel CPU inference Figure 6, GPU Table 1, GPU Figure 12, and code listings. It relocates network diagrams and several retained experimental plots to appendices, and transposes v2's segmentation Table 1 into the horizontal display labeled Figure 2.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's matrix-only experiments, v3 supplies direct single-token LLM timings, response-equivalence checks, implementation details, and explicit storage limitations, improving support and precision of the practical claims. The net gain is limited by the missing update in Algorithm 3 and inconsistencies between new GPU speedup summaries and displayed values, notably Figure 12's 2.87x maximum versus the text's 'up to 2x'.
